title: Generalizable Lithographic Hotspot Detection Using Asynchronous Meta-Learning with Only One Shot
problem: CNN-based lithographic hotspot detectors overfit and fail to generalize to unseen circuit layouts despite being trained on existing designs, limiting applicability across diverse design styles at the same technology node.
method: A few-shot meta-learning framework using asynchronous multi-task learning with a multi-gate mixture-of-experts (MMoE) model that separately updates CNN feature extraction and classification components. Layout topology-based sampling strategy enhances few-shot adaptation, enabling rapid generalization to new designs with only one training layout clip.

title: PoP-ECC: Robust and Flexible Error Correction against Multi-Bit Upsets in DNN Accelerators
problem: Continuous process scaling increases memory error severity and frequency in DNN accelerators, particularly multi-bit upsets (MBUs). Traditional single-error correction codes are insufficient for safety-critical systems.
method: Parities of Parities ECC (PoP-ECC) is a two-tier memory protection scheme. First level computes Virtual Parities (VPs) from data; second level computes Parities of Parities (PPs) from VPs. This hierarchical structure enables dynamic error correction tailored to varying error patterns with minimal overhead.

title: Tackling ML-based Dynamic Mispredictions using Statically Computed Invariants for Attack Surface Reduction
problem: ML-based runtime predictors used for code debloating and dynamic control flow monitoring lack guarantees that distinguish mispredictions from actual security attacks, making them unsuitable for safety-critical security contexts. Without this distinction, the system either blocks legitimate executions (false positives from mispredictions) or fails to stop real attacks.
method: The paper computes static program invariants at compile/analysis time to reduce the attack surface that ML-based dynamic predictors must cover. Statically proven safe behaviors are removed from the ML decision space, so the ML model only makes predictions over a reduced, ambiguous region. When the ML predictor fires on the reduced set, the probability that it is a misprediction versus an actual attack is much lower, enabling more reliable enforcement in security settings such as control flow integrity and debloating.

title: REACT3D: Real-time Edge Accelerator for Incremental Training in 3D Gaussian Splatting based SLAM Systems
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) SLAM requires incremental training and rendering at over 30 FPS on edge devices, but existing GPU-based solutions and prior accelerators fall short due to redundant training computation, unnecessary loss computation, and irregular memory access patterns. The combination of continuous camera streaming, per-Gaussian gradient accumulation, and sparse activated Gaussian sets creates severe compute and memory irregularity.
method: REACT3D introduces two algorithmic optimizations: (1) spatial consistency and convergence-aware sparsification that predicts under-optimized Gaussians based on spatial coherence and convergence dynamics, eliminating redundant forward/backward rendering passes; and (2) a pixel block-wise fine-grained dataflow that fuses loss computation into the rendering pipeline, removing explicit loss storage. At the architectural level, a Content Addressable Memory (CAM)-based Dual-index Gaussian Buffer resolves discontinuous memory accesses by maintaining two parallel indices into the Gaussian buffer, avoiding computation conflicts during gradient merging across scattered Gaussian-to-pixel mappings.

title: An Enhanced-Frequency-Splitting-Based Wireless Power and Data Transfer System Achieving 60.2% End-to-End Efficiency and 1 Mb/s Data Rate with a Sub-cm RX Coil for Miniaturized Implants
problem: Miniaturized implantable devices face a fundamental trade-off between power transfer efficiency (PTE) and data rate (DR) in wireless power and data transfer (WPDT) systems, worsened by coil size constraints; frequency-splitting-based WPDT reduces this trade-off but still requires large receiver coils to achieve critical coupling coefficient, limiting implant miniaturization.
method: Enhanced-frequency-splitting WPDT (EFS-WPDT) system with dynamically controlled receiver LC tank enables Frequency Splitting Enhancement (FSE). By implementing link-load isolation (LLI) via switched on-resistance, the link sees lower effective load resistance, reducing critical coupling coefficient proportionally to loaded receiver Q. Dual-frequency flat-region FSK (FR-FSK) operation at frequencies f_H and f_L maintains both power transfer and data modulation while dynamic LLI enables efficient operation even with sub-cm receiver coils.

title: A 185.2dB-FoMs 8.7aFrms Zoomed Capacitance-to-Digital Converter with Chopping-Based kT/C Noise Cancellation and Add-Then-Subtract Phase-Domain Lead-Compensation Technique
problem: VCO-based time-domain delta-sigma capacitance-to-digital converters (CDCs) face kT/C sampling noise exacerbation at reduced oversampling ratios and lack efficient feedforward compensation techniques for VCO's intrinsically fused integrator and quantizer.
method: The zoom CDC architecture combines SAR coarse stage with VCO-based time-domain fine stage. It employs: (1) chopping-based kT/C noise cancellation requiring only minimal amplification (vs. conventional methods needing power-hungry amplifiers); (2) add-then-subtract phase-domain lead-compensation technique enabling stable high-order loop without linearity penalties; (3) VCO's intrinsic phase integration obviated the need for OTAs.

title: PIMDup: An Optimized Deduplication Design on a Real Processing-in-Memory System
problem: Data deduplication requires scanning entire datasets during chunking, causing excessive data movement between memory and compute. Conventional architectures (GPUs, FPGAs) suffer from von Neumann bottlenecks; processing-in-memory (PIM) systems face unique constraints including restricted inter-DPU sharing and high DPU-CPU communication overhead.
method: PIMDup optimizes deduplication on UPMEM DPUs through efficient parallelization, DPU-friendly chunking techniques that avoid multiplication, and reduced data transfer volumes between DPU and CPU, maintaining 100% result consistency.

title: Hybrid Embedding Framework for Memory-Efficient Recommendation Systems
problem: Deep learning recommendation models (DLRM) suffer from memory bottleneck of large embedding tables that grow with data scale.
method: The framework distinguishes hot (frequent) and cold (infrequent) embeddings. Hot embeddings are stored in compact lookup tables; cold embeddings are computed via deep hash embedding (DHE) networks. Hybrid approach minimizes training time while maintaining accuracy.

title: Age-of-Information Minimization for Data Aggregation in Energy-Harvesting IoTs
problem: Energy-harvesting IoT devices struggle to maintain fresh data under energy constraints; existing AoI minimization methods ignore data aggregation scenarios.
method: Proposes energy-adaptive node scheduling algorithm combining offline scheduling and online adjustment to minimize AoI for data aggregation tasks.

title: 15.4 A Neuroprosthetic SoC with Sensory Feedback Featuring Frequency-Splitting-Based Wireless Power Transfer with 200Mb/s 0.67pJ/b Backscatter Data Uplink and Unsupervised Multi-Class Spike Sorting
problem: High-channel neural implants enable prosthetic control but lack closed-loop sensory feedback, limiting stability and requiring steep user learning curves. Traditional external feedback introduces latency; electrical stimulation is viable but must reject stimulation artifacts to avoid false feedback loops.
method: Frequency-splitting wireless power transfer delivers power and data on distinct carriers, eliminating cross-talk. Backscatter uplink (200 Mb/s, 0.67 pJ/bit) conveys neural data with minimal power overhead. On-chip unsupervised multi-class spike sorting classifies neural signals locally, reducing data bandwidth. Stimulation artifact rejection circuit prevents positive feedback loops during simultaneous stimulation and recording.

title: SSFT: Algorithm and Hardware Co-design for Structured Sparse Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
problem: Sparse fine-tuning (SFT) reduces time and memory requirements compared to dense fine-tuning, but GPU implementation underperforms due to irregular sparse data access patterns that modern GPUs cannot efficiently handle, negating computational benefits.
method: SSFT-Alg introduces predictable sparsity patterns reducing memory access overhead and enhancing regularity. SSFT-Hw accelerator optimizes SSFT-Alg with sparsity-aware design avoiding GPU sparse overhead. Co-design balances algorithm structure and hardware capabilities.

title: 3D-TokSIM: Stacking 3D Memory with Token-Stationary Compute-in-Memory for Speculative LLM Inference
problem: LLM autoregressive decoding faces severe memory bandwidth bottleneck from the logic die; 2D memory solutions cannot overcome this due to limited memory-to-logic bandwidth.
method: Proposes 3D-TokSIM combining 3D memory stacking on logic die with token-stationary compute-in-memory (CIM); uses novel token-stationary dataflow to minimize data movement on logic die, reducing power and balancing compute/memory throughput; architecture exploration allocates CIM resources for higher decoding parallelism.

title: DAPPER: A Performance-Attack-Resilient Tracker for RowHammer Defense
problem: Host-side RowHammer mitigation mechanisms rely on shared counter or tracking structures that are vulnerable to Performance Attacks (Perf-Attacks), where adversaries reverse-engineer the shared structure's mapping to artificially inflate DRAM access counters or trigger early resets, degrading performance of co-running benign applications.
method: DAPPER introduces secure hashing to randomize the mapping of DRAM rows to shared tracking structures, preventing adversaries from predicting counter locations. DAPPER-S provides a base secure hashing template using a single hash function. DAPPER-H extends this with double-hashing, novel reset strategies that avoid predictable early resets, and mitigative refresh techniques that piggyback RowHammer mitigations onto scheduled refresh operations to amortize overhead. The combined design uses only 96KB of SRAM per 32GB of DRAM, validated against 57 workloads from SPEC2006, SPEC2017, TPC, Hadoop, MediaBench, and YCSB.

title: Synergistic Die-Level Router for Multi-FPGA System with Time-Division Multiplexing Optimization
problem: Multi-FPGA systems with multiple dies connected via TDM suffer from critical connection delays and routing congestion from super long lines (SLLs) between dies.
method: Die-level router that jointly optimizes routing topology and TDM timing ratios; reduces reliance on SLLs and critical path delays through topology-aware routing decisions.

title: Citadel: Rethinking Memory Allocation to Safeguard Against Inter-Domain Rowhammer Exploits
problem: Rowhammer attacks exploit DRAM's physical row-adjacency to corrupt memory rows belonging to different security domains; hardware mitigations are costly, slow to adopt, and repeatedly circumvented, while software mitigations incur large performance and memory capacity overheads or provide only partial protection.
method: Citadel is a software-based memory allocator that prevents inter-domain Rowhammer by introducing flexible security domains and physically isolating them in disjoint DRAM regions—ensuring no two domains share physically adjacent rows. The allocator tracks DRAM physical row topology and partitions the address space so that domain boundaries are always separated by guard rows or page-aligned gaps. The design supports thousands of simultaneous security domains on server systems with a 7.2% average memory overhead and no measurable performance loss, without requiring hardware changes and remaining deployable on legacy, current, and future DRAM platforms.

title: Device-Aware Test: A Means to Attack Unmodelled Defects (Invited)
problem: Structural testing at advanced technology nodes and for emerging device technologies is insufficient to screen unmodeled defects, resulting in reduced outgoing product quality.
method: Device-Aware Test (DAT) is proposed as a new manufacturing test methodology that goes beyond traditional structural testing by incorporating device-specific models and characteristics to expose unmodeled faults.
